page: Vultr vx1-m-16c-128gb is a memory-optimized cloud compute instance within the VX1 family, providing 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 8 physical AMD EPYC cores running at 2.0 GHz on x86_64 architecture. The configuration supplies 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is limited to 1 GB of local NVMe SSD, and the instance includes 1 complimentary public IPv4 address without discrete GPU acceleration. The processor integrates 32 MB of L3 cache alongside support for vector instructions including AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16.

Benchmark assessments demonstrate distinctive execution characteristics. Single-threaded tasks exhibit strong performance, with stress-ng single-core compute, gzip compression, and bzip3 decompression ranking in the top tier of evaluated systems. Memory throughput registers in the upper 25 percent on PassMark memory benchmarks, supporting 88.71 GB/s in large-block uncached sequential reads and 45.71 GB/s in writes. In contrast, multi-core CPU throughput, Clang compilation, and database processing remain within median baseline ranges. In terms of cost efficiency relative to resources, the instance offers dense memory capacity per core, though overall compute throughput scales in line with standard multi-threaded cloud baselines.

The primary operational tradeoff is the 1 GB local NVMe SSD allocation, requiring networked or external block storage volumes for persistent data-heavy deployments. Given the 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio and high single-threaded efficiency, this instance is configured for in-memory databases, Redis caching layers, text parsing pipelines, and memory-intensive ETL tasks.
